  <section v="12">

    <t s="10">— that the prayer of an individual which the many need is like communal prayer.</t>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Regarding our topic, the redemption of the Alter Rebbe, these three matters apply to him as a divine servant, and through them he was redeemed in peace.

translations.translation: And now, regarding our topic
(the redemption of our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe16),
it is understood
that these three matters — pertain to the divine servant,
namely our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe,
who was redeemed in peace.
And as he writes, "When I read the verse 'He redeemed in peace... I went out in peace,'"
he himself engaged in these three matters while he was imprisoned
(and therefore his reading was effective)
and through this he was redeemed in peace.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: It is puzzling how communal prayer was possible in prison, but the Tzemach Tzedek explains that an individual's prayer needed by the many is like communal prayer.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
how was the service of communal prayer possible while he was in prison?
For the study of Torah, and in the manner of being engaged in it, is also applicable while in prison,
and also engaging in acts of kindness while in prison, as Hillel said,
when he would go to eat,
that he is going to perform kindness with the wretched and poor — that is his own body17,
but how could he pray with a minyan? And the explanation is,
as explained by his holy honor, the Tzemach Tzedek18
(this year19
being the centennial year of his passing)
— that the prayer of an individual which the many need is like communal prayer.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Alter Rebbe explains that "here for an individual" refers to the Yechidah of the soul, and communal prayer also relates to the Yechidah, which is the innerness of Kesser.

translations.translation: And now, the explanation of our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe20
author of the redemption and joy, on the Sages' statement21
"Here for an individual, there for the community,"
that "here for an individual" is the aspect of Yechidah in the soul.
And from the fact that the Gemara compares "there for the community" to the matter of "here for an individual"
(during the Ten Days of Repentance),
it is understood that also the matter of communal prayer
pertains to the aspect of Yechidah.
For in the matter of the Sefiros, it is the aspect of the innerness of Kesser,
as explained in the maamar
(section 13)
that communal prayer is from the aspect of the innerness of Kesser.
And so it is also regarding the matter of engaging in Torah
(the innerness of Torah)
and acts of kindness
(which is above charity)
that they are from the aspect of the innerness of Kesser — which in divine service is the aspect of Yechidah.
